title: DeformMaster: An Interactive Physics-Neural World Model for Deformable Objects from Videos
claim: One model learned from a casual video supports many capabilities: novel actions, material changes, new views, and downstream use.
layout: Left training/inference sidebar plus 2x2 capability gallery, color-coded action arrows
description: The figure has two parts. A narrow left column shows the pipeline at a glance. The top is Training, a filmstrip frame of a person folding a blue cloth, with a robot icon asking 'Underlying physics?' and 'Appearance?'. Below is Inference, a purple rounded box labeled DeformMaster with a green 'Online Real-time' badge. It lists two modules: 'Interactive physics-neural dynamics' and 'Physics-grounded 4D appearance'. On the right is a 2x2 gallery of rendered cloth results. 'Novel long-horizon actions' shows cloth lifted along orange, yellow and blue arrows. 'Novel material parameters' has a Young's Modulus slider from 0.3 to 4, with the soft and stiff cloth deforming differently. 'Novel view synthesis' shows the cloth from NVS 1 and NVS 2 insets. 'Downstream applications' shows a robot arm manipulating cloth. The eye goes first to the colorful cloth renders.
caption: DeformMaster turns a phone-captured monocular video of deformable objects into an online interactive world model. By recovering both underlying physics and high-fidelity appearance, it supports long-horizon rollouts under novel actions, material-parameter variation, and novel-view synthesis, facilitating downstream embodied applications. (https://can-lee.github.io/deformmaster-web/)
abstract: World models for deformable objects should recover not only geometry and appearance, but also underlying physical dynamics, interaction grounding, and material behavior. Learning such a model from real videos is challenging because deformable linear, planar, and volumetric objects evolve under high-dimensional deformation, noisy interactions, and complex material response. The model must infer a physical state from visual observations, roll it forward under new interactions, and render the resulting dynamics with high visual fidelity. We therefore present DeformMaster, a video-derived interactive physics-neural world model that turns real interaction videos into an online interactive model of deformable objects within a unified dynamics-and-appearance framework. DeformMaster preserves structured physical rollout while using a neural residual to compensate for unmodeled effects, grounds sparse hand motion as distributed compliant actuators for hand-continuum interaction, represents material response with spatially varying constitutive experts, and drives high-fidelity 4D appearance from the predicted physical evolution. Experiments on real-world deformable-object sequences demonstrate DeformMaster's ability to roll out future dynamics and render dynamic appearance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while supporting novel action rollout, material-parameter variation, and dynamic novel-view synthesis. Code and video demos are available at the project page: https://can-lee.github.io/deformmaster-web/
